requirement:
Each delivered search page under {cite}`requirements.authoring.result_pages`
MUST have its own `search_id` and independently require `finish_search`.
Fetching another page MUST NOT require finishing an earlier page.
rationale:
The reviewed test adequately covers `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.pagination`. I judged this from the supplied test source alone and did not request any implementation source.

The one test is `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_pages_are_accounted_only_when_delivered_and_replay_stays_closed]`. It runs for both search tools that produce pages, `ripgrep` and `ast_grep`, using a result large enough to span several pages.

**Obligation 1: each delivered page has its own `search_id` and independently requires `finish_search`.**
- The first page's `search_id` parses as a UUID. After the first page, `outstanding_searches()` equals exactly that one id.
- After `next_page` delivers the second page, its `search_id` also parses as a UUID. `assert_ne!` shows it differs from the first page's id.
- `outstanding_searches().len()` is then 2, so both delivered pages are independently outstanding.
- Finishing the second page with `finish_search` succeeds and records one input. `outstanding_searches()` then holds only the first page's id, so each page's accounting is separate.
- Finishing the first page afterwards succeeds and leaves nothing outstanding.
- An undelivered page's id cannot be finished. A tag from an undelivered page is also rejected when used with the first page's id. This confirms that ids and tags are tied to the page that was delivered.

**Obligation 2: fetching another page does not require finishing an earlier page.**
- `pages.next_page(&token)` succeeds while the first page is still unfinished.
- The second page is finished while the first stays outstanding, so finishing order does not matter.
- Replaying the token after the second page is finished still works and does not change the first page's outstanding status.

I found no relevant distinction left untested. Both the `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` paths are exercised. The other paged tools (`list_files`, `outline`, `references`, `habeas`) do not carry `search_id` or `finish_search` accounting, so they do not bear on this requirement. The test has `{test}` markers for the subject.

text: :::{req} search_accounting.pagination
Each delivered search page under {cite}`requirements.authoring.result_pages`
MUST have its own `search_id` and independently require `finish_search`.
Fetching another page MUST NOT require finishing an earlier page.
:::{req} result_pages
A result of the `habeas` line-range form, `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`,
`ast_grep`, or `references` whose serialized JSON exceeds 32 KiB MUST be
returned in pages. The size limit MUST include search UUIDs, tags, and instructions.
Each page MUST hold whole entries of the result's arrays, such
as inputs, matches, nodes, or sites, with its accompanying definitions, in the
result's order, and MUST NOT exceed 32 KiB unless a single entry does, which
then forms a page of its own. Every paged result MUST include:
```text
page: {
total_entries: Integer,
returned_entries: Integer,
next: String?,
`next` MUST be an opaque token when entries remain and null on the last page.
While entries remain, the page MUST also include a `note` saying that more
entries remain and that `next_page` with `next` returns them. The
harness MUST expose a `next_page({ token: String })` tool returning the following
page of the same result, in the same shape. Pages MUST be kept only until the
assessment that requested them finishes; an unknown token, including one from
another assessment, MUST return an explanatory tool error. A result within the
limit MUST be returned whole, without `page`. Only inputs on pages delivered to
the model MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`.
